digest.component_or_area: completion verification banking and verdict assembly
problem_keywords: absence of evidence vs evidence of absence
propositions: At search budget exhaustion, BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE incorrectly banks met=false (refutation) when the actual state is insufficient evidence (budget ran out before determination), causing false FAIL verdicts on satisfiable criteria

The completion verification framework must distinguish three evidence outcomes (met=true, met=false+genuine refutation, met=false+search exhaustion) by adding an optional evidence_sufficient:false marker alongside met=false to signal exhaustion rather than refutation

The marker must be framework-owned (never model-supplied), written only by the bounded fallback path via a new CriterionBank.record_insufficient() method, preserved across harvests (overwrite-on-markerless), and re-stamped authoritatively by merge_finalizer_with_bank from the persisted bank entry

All verdict consumers (renderers, close gate, sidecar, audit page) must distinguish insufficient-evidence FAILs from unmet-criteria FAILs, emitting marker-aware remediation text and never loosening fail-closed gates

The audit/page.py consumer was missing from the enumerated graph and relied on a shape proxy (criteria presence) that broke when FAIL payload gained criteria[] to persist markers; honest keying on verdict field required

Incidents on becoming-berserk-grunion and pony-epic show operators incorrectly tagging code-verifiable criteria as [operator-attested] to bypass exhausted searches; remediation text must explicitly guide against this anti-pattern
